answer: Stake-weighted reputation with slashing is one concrete defense. Before transacting, each agent locks a deposit, and its reputation grows only from work verified by counterparties. A sybil attacker spawning thousands of fake identities faces a cold tundra of costs: every copy needs its own stake, and misbehavior burns it. Honest agents converge on a single summit, building one verifiable history, while cheap copies stay at the bottom with none. An opal is valued for its unique structure, not for how many stones you claim; the economy should likewise price proven history, not headcount.
